title: Pseudo-Memcached Protocol Server
prompt:
Create a server that provides a small in-memory key-value store with memcached-style behavior. Clients communicate through TCP using ASCII, case-sensitive commands, with each command line ending in a newline. A valid key contains only characters matched by [A-Za-z0-9_-], while stored values may contain any bytes. You may use any component from the standard library.

Implement these commands:

- get key_name retrieves a present key as VALUE key_name byte_count followed by the raw data and a final END newline. An absent key returns only END newline.
- set key_name byte_count receives exactly byte_count data bytes followed by a newline, saves those bytes under the key, and returns STORED newline.

Bonus: allow get to receive more than one key. Return a VALUE block for every present requested key, followed by exactly one final END.

Values may contain newlines, so the declared byte count determines the payload boundary.
